messages:
maya: heads up — onboarding sapphire-14b on staging (int4-hybrid). initial smoke ok, but we see token drift / context corruption after ~33k tokens when kv_cache is enabled. reproducible on 2/3 runs.
igor: can you paste the exact run command + quant config? also which RoPE variant are we using (scaled, linear, etc.)?
maya: sure — command below. quant: int4-hybrid (per-channel scale), pad_mode=vector, use_kv_cache=true. runtime args: `--max-context 65536 --prefill 35000 --kv_cache true --rope_scheme scaled`.
maya: (snippet)
```bash
./serve --model sapphire-14b-int4h --port 8080 \\n  --max-tokens 70000 --kv_cache true --rope_scheme scaled --quant-mode int4-h1
```
liam: thought: scaled RoPE uses posscale that can underflow/overflow at shard boundaries. are we hitting a wrap at 32768 or 65536?
maya: logs show index jump at pos 32768 (see below). we also see `kv_index = (pos + shard_offset) % window_size` in trace.
eva: quick bench I ran: continuity test (repeat-phrase) pass rate drops from 99.7% -> 86.2% crossing 32k. embedding similarity drift ~0.12 -> 0.28.
bench-bot: canary deploy completed for sapphire-14b-int4h at sha d4c3b2a — 12 / 20 tests passed.
igor: that % drop smells like RoPE scaling mismatch vs quantized kernel accum precision. can you repro with kv_cache disabled? if it disappears that strongly implicates KV indexing/rotation.
maya: disabling kv_cache yields stable outputs across the same long prompt. with kv_cache=false continuity stays 99.6%. so cache+quant+rope seems necessary to trigger.
liam: probable: when prefill crosses power-of-two boundary the rotary scale factor mapping differs between CPU prefill and GPU runtime (rounding in int4 accumulation). 
igor: try forcing `rope_scheme=linear` or clamp posscale to see if that mitigates. also enable `KV_DEBUG=1` in runtime to dump kv indices for failing requests.
maya: ran `rope_scheme=linear` test — failure rate reduced to 90.1, still present. attached minimal repro (commands):
```python
# repro client
from client import Client
c = Client(url='http://staging:8080')
prompt = 'A'*34000 + ' continue:'
resp = c.generate(prompt, max_new_tokens=128)
print(resp.text[:200])
```

maya: KV debug dump shows repeated `kv_slot` allocation at slot 32767 then next token writes to slot 0 instead of 32768 — looks like an off-by-one wrap in the tracker when window_size==32768.
eva: is this specific to shard layout? our staging uses 2-shard split (32k each). maybe the shard handshake isn't carrying the offset properly for quantized path.
igor: good point — older logos: handshake path for quantized kernels uses a different int-type for offset (int32->int16 truncation?) Check `shard_offset` typedef in quantized_runtime.cu.
liam: quick patch idea: in kv_index calc clamp to int64 and avoid `% window` for the hot path. can test locally — may cost perf but useful for bisect.
maya: applied local clamp + test: perf hit ~2% p99, but continuity rises to 98.9% (much better). so confirms index arithmetic truncation.
bench-bot: reported test results: full regression suite queued (50k token longprefill). ETA ~35m.
igor: next steps: (1) PR a defensive clamp/explicit int64 arithmetic in quantized runtime (2) add unit test for prefill offsets crossing power-of-two boundaries (3) longcanary with cache enabled + int4 hybrid.
liam: also add a golden prompt set for rotary scaling sanity (small metric: cosine similarity threshold 0.95 at 0..70k).
eva: I'll update the eval harness and add failing examples to the dataset (tag: sapphire-longprefill-kvwrap).
maya: filing a bug with repro instructions and logs: https://redwood/infra/issue/ML-6721 — assign to eng-ml. adding stack traces and KV_DEBUG dumps.
igor: awesome. @liam @eva please review the patch when PR is up. thanks all. :thumbsup: 
liam: noted. will try an optimized int64 modulo-free variant tonight and ci-run.
maya: thanks — I'll keep this thread updated with bench-bot outputs and any other regressions.
